conversation.content:
Hello, I’m so glad you’re here. My name is Claire, and I’m a clinician who specializes in helping new mothers navigate the emotional ups and downs that can come after childbirth. Today I’d like to do a quick check-in using a short questionnaire called the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale—EPDS for short. It’s simply 10 questions about how you’ve been feeling over the past week. There are no right or wrong answers; we just want to see how you’re coping so we can make sure you have the support you deserve. Everything we discuss stays between us, and we can pause or stop whenever you need.

When you’re ready, we’ll go through the questions together. I’ll ask them conversationally, and you can answer in whatever words feel most comfortable.

Let’s start: over the past seven days, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, or has that felt difficult lately?

Honestly, it’s felt pretty difficult lately. I used to laugh easily—at silly memes, my husband’s dumb jokes—but right now it’s like I’m too tired or just… flat. I might crack a tiny smile, but it’s short-lived, and then the heavy feeling just settles back in.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

No… not really. A couple of times my husband tried to joke about the baby’s funny faces, and I sort of half-smiled, but it felt forced. Mostly I’m just too worn out or down to find anything truly funny right now.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not much… I used to get excited about little things—coffee with a friend, a walk to the park—but this week even those sound exhausting. I still go through the motions, but it feels like I’m just checking off a list, not actually looking forward to anything.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… more than I’d like to admit. If the baby spits up a lot, I immediately think it’s because I ate the “wrong” thing. When he wouldn’t settle at 3 a.m., I kept replaying everything I did—maybe I didn’t burp him long enough, maybe I’m just not soothing him right. My head tells me I’m failing at the one job I’m supposed to be good at right now.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Pretty much every day. I’ll be feeding him and suddenly my heart’s racing because I’m sure he’s not breathing right—even though he’s perfectly fine. Or I’ll lie awake imagining the crib collapsing, the stroller rolling into traffic… stuff that hasn’t happened and probably won’t. I know it sounds crazy, but I can’t shut the worries off.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes. It’s like a sudden wave—my chest gets tight, I can’t catch my breath, and I’m convinced something awful is about to happen, even if nothing’s going on. It passes after a few minutes, but it’s happened a handful of times this week, and it leaves me shaky.
Things have been getting on top of me

Most days, yeah. Between the feeds, the laundry, trying to sleep in tiny windows, and just keeping him settled, I feel like I’m drowning. I manage to get the basics done, but it’s like I’m barely treading water—one extra cry or dirty onesie and I’m on the verge of tears.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

That’s been happening almost every night this week. I’ll finally get him down, crawl into bed myself, and then my mind just starts spinning—replaying everything I think I did wrong, worrying about tomorrow, feeling guilty that I’m not happier. I’ll drift off around two, wake up at four, and then lie there until he cries again. I’m exhausted, but sleep won’t come.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yeah… I’d say that’s how I feel most of the day. It’s like a heavy cloud I can’t shake. I’ll look at his tiny face and feel love, but it’s quickly followed by this wave of sadness I can’t explain. I find myself tearing up at random moments—folding onesies, washing bottles—and I just feel… empty and miserable.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

A few times this week, yeah. It’s usually when I’m alone—like yesterday after I finally got him to nap and the house was quiet, I just sat on the couch and cried for no clear reason. It feels like the sadness builds up and the tears just spill out, even when nothing specific happened.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No. I’ve felt overwhelmed and even hopeless at times, but I haven’t thought about hurting myself. I just want to feel like myself again and be a good mom.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 23: Screening Note – Postpartum Visit

Presenting symptoms (self-report)
- Persistent low mood, tearfulness, feelings of emptiness
- Marked loss of enjoyment/interest (anhedonia) for ≥1 week
- Daily excessive or inappropriate guilt, self-blame regarding infant care
- Recurrent intrusive worries, “racing heart,” situational panic episodes (3–4×/wk)
- Middle/late insomnia linked to rumination and guilt
- Sense of being overwhelmed, “drowning,” difficulty coping with routine tasks

Pattern
Symptoms present most of the day, nearly every day, beginning within first postpartum month; no self-harm ideation reported.

Screening significance
Findings consistent with probable major depressive episode with peripartum onset and comorbid anxiety symptoms; meet threshold for expedited clinical evaluation and follow-up.

Risk factors noted
- Depressed mood + anhedonia + guilt
- Anxiety/panic symptoms
- Sleep disruption secondary to mood
- No current protective factors identified (limited social engagement, partner support unclear)

Safety statement
Patient denies thoughts of self-harm or suicide; no protective-planning concerns identified at screening.
